Graph transformations

Source: R/graph-transforms.R
graph-transforms.Rd

Functions that return a modified copy of a graph_data object.

Usage

add_self_loops(g, fill_weight = 1)

remove_self_loops(g)

coalesce_edges(g)

induced_subgraph(g, nodes)

as_undirected(g)

normalize_features(g, method = c("standardize", "row"), stats_mask = NULL)

add_degree_features(g, one_hot = FALSE, max_degree = 10L, log = TRUE)

compose_transforms(...)

Arguments

g

A graph_data object.

fill_weight

Weight of new self loops.

nodes

Integer node indices to keep.

method

"standardize" (zero mean, unit variance per column) or "row" (rows sum to one, as in Kipf and Welling 2017).

stats_mask

Logical node mask used to compute column statistics.

one_hot

Use one-hot degree columns capped at max_degree.

max_degree

Cap for one-hot encoding.

log

Use log1p(degree) for the numeric column.

...

Transform functions, applied left to right.

Value

A graph_data object.

Details

  • add_self_loops(): add a loop (i, i) to every node that has none. New loops get weight fill_weight and zero edge features.

  • remove_self_loops(): drop all loops.

  • coalesce_edges(): merge duplicate stored edges, summing weights and averaging edge features; keeps the first label.

  • induced_subgraph(): keep nodes (in the given order) and the edges among them.

  • as_undirected(): turn a directed graph into an undirected one, keeping one entry per unordered pair (attributes of the first occurrence).

  • normalize_features(): standardize or row normalize node features. With stats_mask, means and scales come from those nodes only (for example the training nodes), so no information from held out nodes enters preprocessing.

  • add_degree_features(): append in degree (optionally log scaled) or one-hot degree columns to x.

  • compose_transforms(): chain transforms for graph_dataset().

Examples

g <- graph_data(x = diag(3), edge_index = rbind(c(1, 1, 2), c(2, 2, 3)))
has_duplicate_edges(g)
#> [1] TRUE
g2 <- coalesce_edges(g)
num_edges(g2)
#> [1] 2
num_edges(add_self_loops(g2))
#> [1] 5
